chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq from Muhammad ibn Talha from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Surely Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, honors the children of the ninety [years] and grants modesty to the children of the eighty [years].
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of reaching the ages of eighty and ninety in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the cumulative spiritual merit of longevity, where Allah’s 'modesty' (istihya) signifies a gracious bestowal of rewards for the believer's endurance in worship. This concept reflects the Shia understanding that aging is not merely physical decline but a progressive elevation in divine favor, particularly as one reaches the mature ages of eighty and ninety.
